title: 【うんちく】ぬるいお風呂のお湯（37℃）が沸とうする場所はどこ？ #Shorts
description:
水が沸く温度は、まわりの空気の重さ（気圧）で決まります。地上では100℃ですが、標準の大気で計算すると、富士山の頂上（3,776 m）で87℃、旅客機の高さ（10 km）で66℃。高さ19 kmで気圧が地上の16分の1になると、37℃、体温くらいのお湯が沸とうします。実際の気圧はその日の天気で少し変わります。

アプリ「極限の世界に置いてみたら」（気圧・水圧）に関係する話です。

アプリ: https://sishiya.github.io/manabi-lab/extreme/

しし屋 まなびラボ（ほかのアプリ）: https://sishiya.github.io/manabi-lab/

出どころ: Wagner & Pruss (2002) J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 31: 387（IAPWS-95、水の蒸気圧）・U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976（NOAA・NASA・USAF）。温度はこの2つからの計算です。

声: VOICEVOX:冥鳴ひまり
BGM: "Sneaky Snitch" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com)

en.title: Did you know? At 19 km up, 37 °C water boils #Shorts
en.description:
The temperature at which water boils depends on the air pressure around it. At sea level it is 100 °C, but by the standard atmosphere it drops to 87 °C at the top of Mt. Fuji (3,776 m) and 66 °C at airliner altitude (10 km). At 19 km, where the pressure is 1/16 of sea level, water boils at 37 °C, about body temperature. Real pressure varies a little with the weather. Turn on English subtitles (CC).

Related to the app "In Extreme Worlds" (air and water pressure).

App (in Japanese for now): https://sishiya.github.io/manabi-lab/extreme/

Shishiya Manabi Lab (more apps): https://sishiya.github.io/manabi-lab/?lang=en

Sources: Wagner & Pruss (2002) J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 31: 387 (IAPWS-95, vapor pressure of water); U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 (NOAA, NASA, USAF). Temperatures are calculated from these two.

Voice: VOICEVOX:Meimei Himari
